exercises.title: Remove the fewest intervals so that the rest do not overlap — greedy by END
concepts: sort by end, keep what fits
exercises.problemHtml:
Intervals are half-open [s, e), so [1,2) and [2,3) do not overlap. Complete static int eraseOverlap(int[][] in): the fewest intervals to remove so that the remaining ones are pairwise disjoint. Do not reorder the caller’s array.

Keep as many as possible = activity selection: sort by end, walk through and keep an interval whenever it starts at or after the end of the last kept one. Answer = n − kept. Sorting by start (or by length) fails. The complexity check has 200,000 intervals.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 200,000 intervals) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n log n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) or exponential one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Các khoảng là nửa mở [s, e), nên [1,2) và [2,3) không chồng nhau. Hoàn thiện eraseOverlap(in): số khoảng ít nhất cần bỏ để những khoảng còn lại đôi một rời nhau. Không đổi thứ tự mảng của nơi gọi.

Giữ được nhiều nhất = chọn hoạt động: sắp theo điểm kết thúc, duyệt và giữ một khoảng mỗi khi nó bắt đầu từ điểm kết thúc của khoảng vừa giữ trở đi. Đáp án = n − số giữ. Sắp theo điểm đầu (hay theo độ dài) là sai. Kiểm độ phức tạp có 200.000 khoảng.

⏱ Kiểm độ phức tạp. Một ca chạy code của bạn với input LỚN (n = 200,000 intervals) trong hạn 3 giây. Lời giải O(n log n) xong trong chưa tới một giây trên laptop bình thường; bản O(n²) or exponential cần lâu hơn rất nhiều và ca in TOO SLOW. Hạn đặt rộng có chủ ý — trượt ca này thì do thuật toán, không phải do máy bạn.

exercises.title: Fewest arrows to burst all balloons — and the subtraction-comparator trap
concepts: shoot at the END of the first unburst balloon
exercises.problemHtml:
Balloon [s, e] (closed, values anywhere in the int range) bursts when an arrow is shot at any x with s ≤ x ≤ e. Complete static int arrows(int[][] b): the fewest arrows that burst every balloon. Do not reorder the caller’s array.

Sort by end; shoot at the end of the first balloon not burst yet, which bursts every balloon starting at or before that point. The trap: a comparator (x, y) -> x[1] − y[1] overflows for ends like −2³¹ and 2³¹ − 1 and sorts wrongly — use Integer.compare.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 200,000 balloons) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n log n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) or exponential one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Same greedy as activity selection: the arrow at the earliest end is never worse than any other choice for the balloon that ends first. O(n log n). The overflow trap is real: a subtraction comparator silently breaks the ordering contract and Arrays.sort may even throw "Comparison method violates its general contract".

Bẫy tràn số là thật: bộ so sánh bằng phép trừ âm thầm phá hợp đồng thứ tự và Arrays.sort thậm chí có thể ném "Comparison method violates its general contract".

exercises.title: Arrange numbers to form the largest number — the comparator a + b vs b + a
concepts: custom order: a before b when a+b > b+a
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static String largest(int[] nums) (non-negative ints): concatenate all numbers in the order that gives the largest number, as a string. Examples: {3,30,34,5,9} → 9534330; {10,2} → 210; {121,12} → 12121; {0,0} → 0.

Plain string order puts "30" before "3" and gives 9534303. The right rule: put a before b when the string a + b is greater than b + a. If the result starts with 0, every number is 0 — return "0". The complexity check concatenates 100,000 numbers (use a StringBuilder).

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 100,000 numbers) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n log n · L) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an trying every order, or string += in a loop one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. exercises.problemHtmlVi:

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: If a+b ≥ b+a for neighbours everywhere, no swap of two adjacent numbers can increase the result, and the relation is transitive (it compares a·10^|b| + b with b·10^|a| + a), so sorting with it is valid. O(n log n) comparisons of short strings.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Nếu a+b ≥ b+a với mọi cặp kề nhau thì không phép đổi hai số kề nào làm kết quả lớn hơn, và quan hệ này có tính bắc cầu (nó so a·10^|b| + b với b·10^|a| + a), nên sắp xếp theo nó là hợp lệ. O(n log n) phép so xâu ngắn.

mistakesJson.loi: Collections.reverseOrder() on the strings — "30" > "3", so 30 comes first: 9534303.|||Collections.reverseOrder() trên các xâu — "30" > "3", nên 30 đứng trước: 9534303.

exercises.title: Candy: two greedy passes (left rule, then right rule)
exercises.problemHtml:
Children stand in a row with ratings r[i]. Everyone gets at least 1 candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour gets more candies than that neighbour (equal ratings: no rule). Complete static long candy(int[] r): the smallest total. Examples: {1,0,2} → 5, {1,2,2} → 4, {1,3,4,5,2} → 11.

Pass 1 left → right: if r[i] > r[i−1], c[i] = c[i−1] + 1. Pass 2 right → left: if r[i] > r[i+1], c[i] = max(c[i], c[i+1] + 1) — the max keeps what pass 1 established. Fixing violations again and again until nothing changes is O(n²) on a long descending run; the complexity check has 1,000,000 children.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1,000,000 children) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) (repeating until stable) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static int kthLargest(int[] a, int k) (1 ≤ k ≤ n): the k-th largest value (duplicates count separately: in {3,2,3,1,2,4,5,5,6} the 4th largest is 4). Do not modify a.

exercises.title: Count pairs i < j with a[i] > 2·a[j] — merge sort counting (and the 2L trap)
concepts: two sorted halves: one forward pointer
exercises.problemHtml:
